> \(c\) **Enforcement of Remedies.** Following any delinquency or default by an obligor under a Receivable, the Servicer shall take such action with respect to such Receivable as the Servicer would take in the normal course of its servicing activities for comparable receivables that it services for its own account, including sending notices to obligors, initiating collection calls, engaging collection agencies, repossessing Financed Vehicles, and disposing of repossessed Financed Vehicles in accordance with applicable law.
>
> \(d\) **Customer Service.** The Servicer shall provide customer service to obligors in accordance with its customary servicing standards, including responding to inquiries, processing payment modifications and extensions (subject to the limitations set forth in the Sale and Servicing Agreement), and handling complaints.

**[Section 7.03 --- Servicing Fee]{.underline}**

As compensation for its servicing activities hereunder, the Servicer shall be entitled to receive a monthly Servicing Fee equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of 1.00% per annum of the Pool Balance as of the first day of the related Collection Period. The Servicing Fee shall be payable from Available Funds on each Payment Date as the first priority in the waterfall set forth in Section 5.01(a) (step First). The Servicing Fee is calculated on the basis of the Pool Balance (i.e., the aggregate outstanding principal balance of all Receivables other than Defaulted Receivables) and not on the basis of the Outstanding Note Balance, the Initial Note Balance, or any other amount. The Servicer shall not be entitled to any additional compensation for its servicing activities other than the Servicing Fee, except as expressly provided in the Sale and Servicing Agreement.

**[Section 7.04 --- Servicer Events of Default]{.underline}**

Each of the following events shall constitute a \"Servicer Event of Default\" under this Indenture:

> \(a\) The Servicer shall fail to deposit any collections into the Collection Account within the time period required by Section 4.02 hereof, and such failure shall continue unremedied for a period of five (5) Business Days after the earlier of (i) the date on which written notice of such failure is received by the Servicer from the Indenture Trustee or from holders of at least 25% of the Outstanding Note Balance and (ii) the date on which a Responsible Officer of the Servicer obtains actual knowledge of such failure.
>
> \(b\) The Servicer shall fail to deliver the monthly Servicer report to the Indenture Trustee on any Determination Date as required by Section 7.06 hereof, and such failure shall continue unremedied for a period of five (5) Business Days after written notice thereof is received by the Servicer from the Indenture Trustee.
>
> \(c\) The Servicer shall breach any representation, warranty, or covenant made by it in this Indenture or in the Sale and Servicing Agreement, which breach has a material adverse effect on the Noteholders, and such breach shall not be cured within sixty (60) days after written notice thereof is given to the Servicer by the Indenture Trustee or by holders of at least 25% of the Outstanding Note Balance.
>
> \(d\) The Servicer shall (i) file a petition in bankruptcy or be adjudicated as bankrupt or insolvent, (ii) consent to the appointment of a receiver, liquidator, or trustee of itself or of any part of its property, (iii) admit in writing its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, (iv) make a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or (v) be the subject of an order for relief by any court of competent jurisdiction entered in any involuntary proceeding against it under the federal bankruptcy laws, which order remains unstayed and in effect for sixty (60) days.
>
> \(e\) The Servicer shall make an assignment for the benefit of its creditors, or shall consent to the appointment of a conservator, receiver, or liquidator in any insolvency, readjustment of debt, marshaling of assets and liabilities, or similar proceedings of or relating to the Servicer, or the Servicer shall be adjudicated as bankrupt or insolvent.

**[Section 7.05 --- Appointment of Successor Servicer; Back-Up Servicer]{.underline}**

Upon the occurrence of a Servicer Event of Default, and so long as such Servicer Event of Default shall be continuing, the Indenture Trustee may, and at the written direction of holders of a majority of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Notes of the Controlling Class shall, by notice to the Servicer, terminate all of the rights and obligations of the Servicer under this Indenture and the Sale and Servicing Agreement, and the Indenture Trustee shall appoint a successor Servicer acceptable to the Indenture Trustee to assume all servicing responsibilities.

Granite Loan Servicing LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, has been appointed as the Back-Up Servicer pursuant to the Back-Up Servicing Agreement, dated as of November 15, 2024. The Back-Up Servicer shall, at all times during the term of this Indenture, maintain operational readiness, including maintaining updated copies of the Receivables data tapes, verifying the integrity of such data, and ensuring the capability of its systems to assume full servicing responsibilities, so as to be able to assume active servicing duties within thirty (30) days of receipt of notice from the Indenture Trustee or the Controlling Class directing it to assume such duties.

The Back-Up Servicer Fee shall be \$5,000 per month, equivalent to \$60,000 per annum. The Back-Up Servicer Fee shall be payable to Granite Loan Servicing LLC only upon the activation of back-up servicing duties --- that is, only upon the Back-Up Servicer\'s assumption of active servicing responsibilities following the termination of the Servicer. During any period in which the Back-Up Servicer is in standby mode and has not assumed active servicing duties, the Back-Up Servicer Fee shall not be payable and is not included as a priority in the Section 5.01 waterfall. Upon activation of the Back-Up Servicer, the Back-Up Servicer Fee shall be payable on each Payment Date as an additional component of the Servicing Fee under step First of the Section 5.01 waterfall.

The Back-Up Servicer shall have no liability hereunder for any action taken or omitted to be taken during the period prior to its assumption of active servicing duties, except for its obligation to maintain operational readiness as described above.

**[Section 7.06 --- Servicer Reporting]{.underline}**

On each Determination Date (the tenth (10th) day of each month, or the next succeeding Business Day if such day is not a Business Day), commencing December 10, 2024, the Servicer shall deliver to the Indenture Trustee a monthly servicer report (the \"Servicer Report\") containing the following information with respect to the related Collection Period:

> \(a\) total collections received, broken down by scheduled principal, scheduled interest, prepayments, and Liquidation Proceeds; (b) the number and aggregate principal balance of Receivables that became Defaulted Receivables during such Collection Period; (c) delinquency information (31--60 days, 61--90 days, 91--120 days, 120+ days); (d) the Annualized Default Rate and the three-month rolling average thereof; (e) the Cumulative Net Loss Rate; (f) the Pool Balance as of the last day of such Collection Period; (g) the OC Amount and comparison to the Target OC Amount and Minimum OC Amount; (h) the Reserve Account balance and comparison to the Reserve Account Required Balance; (i) the results of Trigger Event testing; and (j) such other information as the Indenture Trustee may reasonably request.

In the event of such resignation, the Issuer shall promptly appoint a successor Indenture Trustee, subject to the approval of the holders of a majority of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Notes of the Controlling Class.

The Indenture Trustee may be removed at any time by the holders of a majority of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Notes of the Controlling Class, by notice in writing to the Indenture Trustee, the Issuer, and the Servicer, for cause (including the failure of the Indenture Trustee to perform its duties hereunder, insolvency of the Indenture Trustee, or the appointment of a receiver for the Indenture Trustee).

No resignation or removal of the Indenture Trustee shall become effective until a successor Indenture Trustee has been appointed and has accepted such appointment in accordance with Section 11.05.

**[Section 11.05 --- Successor Indenture Trustee]{.underline}**

Any successor Indenture Trustee appointed pursuant to Section 11.04 shall be a national banking association or state-chartered bank or trust company organized under the laws of any state of the United States, with a combined capital and surplus of at least \$500,000,000 and subject to supervision or examination by federal or state authority. If such entity publishes reports of condition at least annually, pursuant to law or to the requirements of federal or state supervising or examining authority, then for the purposes of this Section 11.05, the combined capital and surplus of such entity shall be deemed to be its combined capital and surplus as set forth in its most recent report of condition so published.

Upon the appointment and acceptance of a successor Indenture Trustee, the retiring Indenture Trustee shall promptly transfer all property and documents held by it as Indenture Trustee to the successor Indenture Trustee, and the successor Indenture Trustee shall thereupon succeed to and become vested with all the rights, powers, trusts, and duties of the retiring Indenture Trustee under this Indenture.

**[ARTICLE XII --- OPTIONAL REDEMPTION]{.underline}**

**[Section 12.01 --- Optional Redemption (Clean-Up Call)]{.underline}**

The Servicer may, at its option, redeem all (but not less than all) Outstanding Notes on any Payment Date on or after the first Payment Date on which the Pool Balance has declined to an amount equal to or less than 10% of the Initial Pool Balance. The Initial Pool Balance is \$712,300,000; accordingly, the optional redemption may be exercised on or after the first Payment Date on which the Pool Balance has declined to \$71,230,000 or less (\$712,300,000 multiplied by 10% equals \$71,230,000).

The redemption price (the \"Redemption Price\") for each class of Notes shall be equal to the sum of:

> \(a\) the outstanding principal amount of such class of Notes as of the redemption date;
>
> \(b\) all accrued and unpaid interest on such class of Notes to but excluding the redemption date; and
>
> \(c\) a *pro rata* share (based on the outstanding principal amount of such class of Notes relative to the aggregate outstanding principal amount of all Notes) of all amounts then owed to the Indenture Trustee (including the Indenture Trustee Fee and any unreimbursed expenses) and to the Servicer (including the Servicing Fee) under the transaction documents.

The Servicer shall exercise its optional redemption right by delivering written notice (the \"Redemption Notice\") to the Indenture Trustee and to all Noteholders (or, so long as the Notes are held in book-entry form, to DTC for distribution to its participants) at least thirty (30) days prior to the Payment Date on which the redemption is to be effected. The Redemption Notice shall specify (i) the Payment Date on which the redemption will occur, (ii) the Redemption Price for each class of Notes, and (iii) that all Notes will be redeemed on such date.

The Servicer shall deposit or cause to be deposited into the Collection Account, on or before the Business Day immediately preceding the redemption date, an amount equal to the aggregate Redemption Price for all classes of Notes, plus all amounts owed to the Indenture Trustee and the Servicer. On the redemption date, the Indenture Trustee shall distribute the Redemption Price to each class of Noteholders in accordance with the priority set forth in Section 5.01 (applying payments first to interest and then to principal in the order of seniority specified therein).

The obligation to pay the Redemption Price shall be unconditional and irrevocable upon delivery of the Redemption Notice. Once a Redemption Notice has been delivered, the Servicer may not rescind or withdraw such notice.

**[Section 12.02 --- Effect of Redemption]{.underline}**

Upon payment of the Redemption Price in full for all classes of Notes, all Notes shall be deemed paid in full and shall be cancelled. The Indenture Trustee shall, at the written request of the Issuer, execute and deliver such instruments as may be necessary to release the Trust Estate from the lien of this Indenture and to reconvey the Trust Estate to the Issuer (or to the Certificateholder, as directed by the Issuer).

Following such release and reconveyance, the Trust shall be wound up and terminated in accordance with the Trust Agreement, and any remaining assets of the Trust (including any amounts in the Reserve Account in excess of amounts owed to the Indenture Trustee and the Servicer) shall be distributed to the Certificateholder.

def table(headers, rows, widths=None, header_fill="1F2A44", fontsize=9):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ""
        r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(fontsize); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF)
        shade(c, header_fill)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            r = cells[i].paragraphs[0].add_run(str(v)); r.font.size = Pt(fontsize)
            if headers[i] == "Severity" and v in SEVCOL:
                r.bold = True; r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(SEVCOL[v])
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# I. Executive Summary

Bottom line: the November 18 Offering Memorandum (the "OM") should not be distributed further, used for pricing on November 25, or incorporated into roadshow materials until it is corrected. Our systematic, section-by-section comparison against the executed Indenture identified 50 discrepancies and omissions in the OM (6 Critical, 16 High, 16 Medium and 12 Low), plus 7 drafting points in the Indenture itself that should be resolved before closing on November 27. Both issues raised in Terrence's November 20 email are confirmed; however, they are only two of six Critical items, and several of the most significant problems are in sections that were not reviewed in the preliminary pass.

The Critical items, each of which goes to the economics or the rated credit structure of the Notes, are:

- **A-1:** Class C Note interest rate stated as 6.50% in Description of the Notes (Associate Issue 2 --- CONFIRMED)

- **A-2:** Interest day-count convention --- OM states actual/360; Indenture provides 30/360 for every class (NOT flagged by associate)

- **A-3:** Final Scheduled Payment Dates differ for all five classes

- **B-1:** Reserve Account replenishment placed ahead of Class B and Class C principal (Associate Issue 1 --- CONFIRMED, with citation corrections)

- **C-1:** Minimum OC Amount --- fixed \$10,684,500 (1.50% of initial pool) in OM vs. 1.50% of current Pool Balance in Indenture

- **D-1:** "Defaulted Receivable" --- 90 days/repossession in OM vs. 120 days in Indenture

Among the High items, two warrant particular attention because they may reflect a problem in the Indenture rather than the OM: (i) the OM's description of an overcollateralization target with release of excess spread to the Certificateholder has no corresponding mechanic in Indenture §5.01(c), whose Principal Distribution Amounts sweep all remaining Available Funds to principal every month (B-5/K-7); and (ii) the 90-day/repossession versus 120-day "Defaulted Receivable" definition (D-1), which drives every performance trigger. For those items, and for the Minimum OC Amount (C-1), the CNL table (E-1) and the 72- versus 75-month term representation (G-1), the threshold question is which document reflects the negotiated deal and Kensington's model --- the answer determines whether the OM is conformed or the Indenture is amended before closing.

Governing principle. The Indenture is the operative instrument, and the OM's own conflict clause provides that the transaction documents control. That clause does not cure a disclosure problem: an OM that misdescribes the coupon, day count, maturities, waterfall, triggers or credit enhancement is materially misleading for purposes of Rule 10b-5 regardless of what the Indenture provides, and would undermine the 10b-5 negative assurance letters expected from this firm and Blackthorn & Kessler LLP. Unless the business parties confirm that the Indenture is wrong on a given point, our recommendation is to conform the OM to the Indenture.

### Severity Scale

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Severity**                        **Meaning**
  ----------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Critical**                        Misstates a core economic or rated structural term (coupon, day count, maturity, priority of payments, trigger/OC base, default definition). Must be corrected before any further distribution or pricing.

  **High**                            Material misdescription or omission likely to affect an investor's or the rating agency's analysis (fees, reserve mechanics, CNL level, servicing/back-up servicing, R&W scope, call threshold, pool count). Correct before pricing.

  **Medium**                          Inaccurate or incomplete description of a contractual mechanic or defined term; correct in the revised OM.

  **Low**                             Conforming, presentation or administrative point; correct in the revised OM.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# II. Scope, Documents Reviewed and Methodology

Documents reviewed in full:

- **OM.** Confidential Offering Memorandum, Crescent Auto Receivables Trust 2024-2, \$687,500,000 Asset-Backed Notes, dated November 18, 2024 (all sections, Glossary and Appendix A).

- **Indenture.** Indenture dated as of November 15, 2024 between Crescent Auto Receivables Trust 2024-2 and Halcyon National Trust Company, as Indenture Trustee and Paying Agent (Articles I--XV, Collateral Pool Summary, Schedule I and Exhibit A).

- **Associate email.** Email from Terrence L. Gage to Samantha K. Everett dated November 20, 2024 ("CART 2024-2: Preliminary OM/Indenture Discrepancies --- Need Full Review").

Methodology. Every OM section was walked against the corresponding Indenture provisions, covering each area the associate identified as outstanding: defined terms (OM Glossary vs. Indenture §1.01); Trigger Events and the CNL table; credit enhancement (OC and Reserve Account); servicing provisions and fee calculations; representations and warranties; transfer restriction and securities-law language; collateral pool statistics and receivable count; and the clean-up call. We also re-checked the two flagged issues, recomputed all stated percentages and dollar figures, and checked the OM for internal inconsistencies (including between the Summary of Terms and the body). Cross-references in this report are to Indenture section numbers and OM section headings (the OM page numbers in the table of contents could not be verified against the electronic draft).

Limitations. We have not reviewed the Sale and Servicing Agreement, the Amended and Restated Trust Agreement, the Back-Up Servicing Agreement, the Placement Agreement, the Kensington rating presale/letters, the Saxonbrook agreed-upon procedures letter or the data tape. Several items below (notably G-2, G-3 and the Servicer provisions) should be confirmed against the Sale and Servicing Agreement, which the Indenture references for capitalized terms not defined in it and which may contain additional representations.

# III. Verification of the Associate's Flagged Issues

## Issue 1 --- Reserve Account Replenishment Priority: CONFIRMED (see B-1)

The OM Flow of Funds places Reserve Account replenishment at step (10), between Class A-3 principal (9) and Class B principal (11). The Indenture places it at step Thirteenth of §5.01(a), after principal on all classes (Eighth through Twelfth), and twice restates that replenishment "is subordinated in priority to all principal payments on the Notes" (§4.04; §6.02). Terrence's analysis of the consequence is correct: the OM ordering would subordinate Class B and Class C principal to reserve replenishment, which misdescribes the credit enhancement for the mezzanine and subordinate classes and is a rating-methodology-sensitive feature.
